column3: **Phase 3b skill source: which mechanism pins each controller's skills to the promoted SHA?** The Phase 3a spike (iteration 34, PASS 88, `fleet-mission-evidence/iteration34/phase3b-decision.md`) measured: claude user-level `~/.claude/skills` beats every project copy and `--add-dir`; a per-fire `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` keeps auth (env token) and its `skills/` wins. Codex reads `.agents/skills` + `$CODEX_HOME/skills` (CODEX_HOME wins), never `.claude/skills`; a per-fire CODEX_HOME needs a credential copy. pi: explicit `--skill` + `/skill:` only. **A (recommended):** retire the user-level mission-skill symlinks so the cwd=pin project copy resolves; World gets `--add-dir <pin>`; codex reads the pin's `.agents` mirror under a parity check (#544 becomes a gate) with `$CODEX_HOME/skills` free of mission names; pi gets `--skill <abs pin path>` per skill. Cost: attended sessions outside a checkout lose these skills. **B:** per-fire config dirs (claude `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`; codex needs a credential-copy ruling); every fire must replicate settings, hooks and memory. **C:** no change for skills; Phase 3b promotes driver + binary only, and skills stay on the D-FLEET-15 fast-forward. Default if unanswered: C.

**Dev's REQUIRED checks have been red since 2026-10-13 20:02Z, from causes outside fleet scope, and the owner (V1) has been disabled since 09-14. No PR to dev can merge, including fleet #1824 (judged PASS 88). Who fixes it?** Causes, measured by the controller and the judge: (1) `test`: `make check-git-exec` refuses 2 bare `git` exec sites, `internal/executor/managed_agents/devapi_workspace.go:237,259` (`ffef3402a`). (2) `docs-gate`/`docs-build`: an MDX/acorn error at `docs/docs/reference/env-vars.md:252`, the `'{"sort":"throughput"}'` example, generated from `internal/config/ai.go:43`. (3) Not required: `Build windows-latest` fails 2 tests in the same package. **A (recommended):** an attended session fixes (1) and (2) now. Route both git calls through `internal/gitexec` (or add a `scripts/git_exec_baseline.txt` row), and escape or reword the brace example in `ai.go`, then regenerate. Each is a small diff. **B:** grant the fleet a narrow standing authority to fix a REQUIRED-check red on dev when the owning mission's kill switch is set. Such a fix ships alone, is judged by an evaluator, and passes the done-gate. **C:** no change; the fleet keeps building and parks every landing. Default if unanswered: C.

**`messaging:pubsub-notify-wrong-project` (world, 10-15) is outside fleet scope. Who fixes it, and how?** Measured at iteration 42: `notifyConfigForStore` (`cmd/ailang/messages_send.go:742`) already publishes to the store's project. The project in the error, `sunholo-gemini-enterprise`, is the `quota_project_id` of the rig's ADC credential (`~/.config/gcloud/application_default_credentials.json`), so Pub/Sub calls are billed to a project with the API disabled. The store write succeeds; only the notification fails. **A (recommended):** an attended session runs `gcloud auth application-default set-quota-project ailang-multivac` on the rig, after checking that nothing else on the rig (the GE executor work) relies on that quota project. **B:** a code fix in `cmd/ailang`/`internal/messaging` to pass `option.WithQuotaProject(<store project>)` to the Pub/Sub client. That is V1's lane, outside the fleet allowlist. **C:** no change; notifications from the rig keep failing silently, and the store still receives messages. Default if unanswered: C, and the ticket stays open.

**`quorum:gpt6-1-sol-openai-api-credits-exhausted` (world, 10-01): the design-quorum's OpenAI seat bills the OpenAI API key, which has no credits, so the seat is ABSENT (`openai error (429): You have no credits remaining`) whenever it is seated. Which fix?** Measured at iteration 43: the seat is `gpt6-1-sol` (`cmd/ailang/design_quorum.go:183`, provider `openai` in `internal/modelreg/models.yml:577`). Of the 15 artifacts in `~/.ailang/state/mission-quorum`, the seat appears in 10 (world, 2026-10-02T18:45–19:31Z), and all 10 list it in `absent_reviewers` as `unreachable`. The two 10-14 fleet quorums did not seat it. The reserve `gemini-4-argon` fills in, so every quorum still has 3 seats, but none of them is OpenAI. `codex exec gpt-6.1-sol` on the ChatGPT subscription works (probe rc 0 this fire). Both fixes are outside fleet scope (`cmd/ailang`, billing). **A (recommended):** route the quorum's OpenAI seat through the subscription `codex exec` lane, as the roles already do. This is a routing/billing change in `cmd/ailang/design_quorum.go` (V1 lane or attended), with $0 metered. **B:** top up the OpenAI API org's credit; there is no code change, and the seat bills metered dollars again. **C:** no change; the reserve keeps filling the seat, and quorums stay without an OpenAI vendor (quoted as N-1). Default if unanswered: C, and the ticket stays open.

**Gate 3b's CI poll cap (1800 s) is now shorter than dev CI. Raise it?** Measured twice. Iteration 43: dev CI runs took 31–55 min, and the PR poll timed out at 30 min with 1 check pending. Iteration 44: the PR poll timed out at 30 min with `build` pending and 0 failures, and a second poll went green minutes later. Each timeout costs a second poll and, read literally, PARKs a green run. The snippet's comment still says "CI is ~15-20m". Standing rule 6 sets a ≤30-min default for any wait, so this is a time-budget call, not a mechanical fix. **A (recommended):** raise the Gate 3b poll cap to 3600 s, with the Bash tool `timeout` at 3800000 ms (the tool allows 7200000), in both copies of `resources/gate-3b-ci-green.md`. Correct the CI-duration comment, and name Gate 3b as an exception to rule 6's 30-min default. **B:** keep 1800 s, but prescribe one automatic re-poll on a fresh path when the only pending checks are still running and none has failed (what iterations 43 and 44 did by hand). **C:** no change; the controller keeps re-polling by hand. Default if unanswered: C. **Iteration 80 (2026-11-03): option A is built as a proposed diff, draft PR #2067** (head `bdaad2825`): 7 lines per `gate-3b-ci-green.md` copy (cap 3600 s, tool `timeout` 3800000 ms, comment "CI median ~15 min, tail past 30 min") and one in-place clause in standing rule 6, both mirrors byte-identical; independent sonnet judge PASS 90. Re-measured: over 200 CI runs 10-28..11-03 the median is ~15 min, 23 ran over 30 min and 7 over 60 (max 99, 10-29); so A covers most of the tail and B covers the rest.

**`reporting:daneel-reports-not-declared-triage` (triage, 10-16) is outside fleet scope. Who declares the inbox?** A prod `ailang messages send daneel-reports` is refused (`no agent serves "daneel-reports" and it is not declared human-triage`, `cmd/ailang/messages_send_inbox_guard.go:52`). Daneel polls that inbox (`~/dev/daneel/config/report-inboxes.tsv`, `schedule.tsv` hourly :35), so it does have a consumer. The declaration is the coordinator config key `triage_only_inboxes` (`internal/coordinator/daemon_tasks_init.go:131`). For prod that lives in the multivac repo's cloud config, which no fleet path reaches. The triage loop works around it by reporting to `controlplane`. **A (recommended):** an attended session adds `daneel-reports` to `triage_only_inboxes` in the prod coordinator config and rolls the coordinator revision; the registry loads once, so a config push alone does not apply. **B:** Daneel reads `controlplane` instead, and the triage loop keeps today's workaround; no config change. **C:** no change; the ticket stays open. Default if unanswered: C.

**The rest of `crash:sprint-executor:sigbus-ram-tmp-full-make-test` is outside fleet scope. Who fixes it?** Ask 1 landed (#1905). **Two of your rulings disagree on `gpt-6-luna`; confirm which stands.** D-FLEET-12 item 1 (2026-10-02) says mission roles may spawn only `gpt-6.1-sol` among OpenAI models. The triage charter (`design_docs/triage-mission.md` § Routing policy, ratified with you 2026-10-15) routes its read-only verifiers to `codex:gpt-6-luna`; `~/.config/ailang/mission-triage.env:24,33` pins it as triage's executor and controller fallback, and triage is armed. Docs pins it as well (2026-09-30; docs is disabled). Iteration 53 built the allowlist as **`gpt-6.1-sol` + `gpt-6-luna`**: the later statement wins on the point of conflict (gate-0 rule 6(g)), and the literal list would have demoted triage's ratified verifier lane at the next binary rebuild. Astra, `gpt-6-sol` and every `gpt-5.6-*` stay refused. **A (recommended, as shipped):** keep luna allowed. It is the current GPT-6 small tier at $0.10/$0.50 per 1M, not a retired model. **B:** remove luna. Delete it from `AllowedOpenAIModels` (`internal/mission/quorum/rolemodels.go`) and from `ALLOWED_OPENAI` in `scripts/mission_routing_models_check.sh`; a parity test holds the two together. Then move triage's and docs' luna rungs to `codex:gpt-6.1-sol`, which is an attended env edit. Default if unanswered: A, as shipped.

**`quorum:claude-p-ration-usage-429` (stapledon, 10-21, `blocking=item`): the design-quorum's Anthropic seat is refused whenever subscription usage cannot be read, and it cannot be read now. Which fix?** Measured at iteration 56 on `d25d9b8d0`; a sonnet judge reproduced it first-party. (1) The usage endpoint returns HTTP 429 (`ailang mission quota --bucket anthropic` prints `unknown [ENFORCED]`). The cause is unmeasured. (2) The CLI fallback is dead. Claude Code 2.1.308 answers `claude -p /usage` with a session cost summary only, so `internal/mission/anthropic_usage_cli.go` can never match. No other non-inference route to the usage windows was found (`/status` is unavailable in `-p`; stream-json carries no rate-limit fields). (3) The seat gate, `cmd/ailang/design_quorum.go:192`, refuses on `Blocked()`, which is true for `unknown` as well as `over`. The driver's own tested rule is the opposite: an unreadable quota is probed, not refused (`tools/launchd/test_anthropic_quota_admission.sh`). `design_quorum.go` is outside fleet scope. Changing `Blocked()` would change admission and `quota --over`, which is HD-2a. The block stops Stapledon's Kerr re-quorum, because its D-107 A needs an Anthropic or OpenAI seat. **A (recommended):** an attended or V1 change makes the seat refuse only on a measured `over` and run on `unknown`, matching the driver. That is a few lines plus a test. **B:** Stapledon runs that quorum with `AILANG_ANTHROPIC_RATION=0` for the one invocation. No code changes, but the seat would also run on a bucket that really is over. **C:** no change; the seat stays absent until the endpoint answers. Default if unanswered: C.

**Fleet Go fixes do not reach the loops, because nothing rebuilds the binary they run. Who rebuilds it, and when?** Every mission runs `~/go/bin/ailang`, which `mission-control.sh:68` puts first on PATH. Measured at iteration 56: that binary was built 2026-10-19 from `128371f` (`vcs.modified=true`). Three landed fleet Go fixes are newer: #1912 `3b4d11759` (rotate-log heading shapes), #1917 `9aebccf9b` (opencode is not a quota pool) and #1922 `d75ef77f5` (OpenAI role allowlist in `codex-exec` and quorum seating; its shell half does reach). Stapledon re-filed #1912's defect as `rotate-log:heading-parse-stapledon` because its fire ran the 10-19 binary. On a scratch copy, the old binary reproduces "9 of 9 kept, 0 rotated", and a HEAD build rotates correctly. Log entries since iteration 32 have recorded "reaches loops at the next rebuild or release" as a caveat; this is the first ticket that caveat produced. **A (recommended):** an attended `make quick-install` on the rig now, at a moment with no eval running (evals share that binary; never `cp` over it). After that, rebuild after each merged fleet Go fix until Phase 3b promotes the binary per fire (D-FLEET-16). **B:** the fleet may change the driver to build a binary from the pin each fire and put it first on PATH for the loop only, while evals keep `~/go/bin`. That pulls forward Phase 3b's binary half, and it needs your ruling because it changes what every loop executes. **C:** no change; Go fixes reach loops only at a release. Default if unanswered: C.

**`quorum:oc-glm-5-3-output-cap-invalid` (stapledon, 10-21): the diagnosis half is fixed. Should the quorum also stop spending reasoning tokens that yield no verdict?** Measured at iteration 62: 2 of 23 banked `oc-glm-5-3` seatings ran to exactly 65,536 output tokens (the `max_output_tokens` it is called with) and returned an empty body. A third run of the same 55 KB doc succeeded at 56,487 tokens. The cost is $0.63 imputed. Ollama Cloud is flat-rate, so that is quota, not metered money. #1966 (`0802749cb`) makes such a seat read `truncated … inferred from tokens_out 65536 >= max_output_tokens 65536` instead of "malformed JSON". The waste itself is policy. **A (recommended):** no further change. The seat is the reserve, the quorum already degrades to N-1, and the error is now legible. **B:** after one cap hit, do not re-seat that reviewer in the same fire (`internal/mission/quorum/seating.go`, inside fleet scope; seating policy, HD-2a). Saves about a run's quota, and loses the chance that a re-run succeeds, as the third kerr run did. **C:** raise `oc-glm-5-3`'s `max_output_tokens` (`internal/modelreg/models.yml`, outside fleet scope), only if GLM-5.3 on Ollama Cloud accepts more. That is unmeasured. It fits the full-ability policy on `reviewerMaxTokens`. Not offered: lowering the cap or adding a reasoning budget, because restricting thinking is reserved to evals. Default if unanswered: A. The ticket stays open until this is answered.

**`quota:admission-has-no-headroom-margin-and-flaps` (attended, 10-02) is a ghost for 3 of its 4 asks. Should ask 3, an in-run spend cap, still be built?** Measured at iteration 65 on `58a41bad4`; an independent sonnet judge confirmed it from the code (PASS 86). Attended #1524 (`71eec62b6`, "Resolves harness ticket …") and #1616 (`134e02999`) built ask 1 as fixed per-bucket start margins (`internal/mission/quota_margin.go`: codex 2pp, anthropic 1pp, ollama 3pp, openrouter $0.60). These are the margins D-FLEET-12 rules, in place of the ticket's rolling per-mission p75. Ask 2 (hysteresis) holds by construction, because every fire re-tests `headroom >= margin`. Ask 4 (fallback rungs) holds, because every controller rung, lane probe and role spawn reads the same `ailang mission quota --over` verdict (`tools/launchd/lib/lane-probe.sh:192`). **Ask 3 is not built.** Quota is read once per fire (`MISSION_OVER_RATION`, `mission-control.sh:2302`), so nothing stops a run mid-way. The ticket's evidence is one run, World iteration 217, which spent 24pp of the weekly Codex bucket. Changing it is quota policy (HD-2a). **A:** the fleet designs an in-run cap (a per-run pp ceiling read at gate boundaries; the controller records and exits cleanly past it). **B (recommended):** waive ask 3 and resolve the ticket, citing `71eec62b6`. The margins now block the next fire after an overrun. An in-run abort discards work mid-flight, which is the failure this loop guards hardest against. The measured demand is one run. **C:** no change; the ticket stays open. Default if unanswered: C.

**`pi:unowned-dirty-absolute-vs-relative-paths` (interactive, 10-02) is real at HEAD, and its fix is a `.pi/extensions/**` change, so it parks per D-FLEET-3. Approve the diff?** Measured at iteration 66 on `c0458fdfd`. An independent sonnet judge confirmed all four load-bearing claims (verdict PARTIAL, on one objection that the diff now covers). The defect: `.pi/extensions/unowned-dirty.ts:42` and `:78` store the session's own files as absolute paths, while `unownedDirty()` compares them with repo-relative `git status --porcelain` paths, so every own edit is reported as unowned. The proposed diff ([`unowned-dirty-proposed.diff`](fleet-mission-evidence/iteration66/unowned-dirty-proposed.diff)) adds `relativeTo(top, paths)` (the contract of the Claude Code port in `tools/claude-mods/unowned-dirty`), runs `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` before the status read, and realpaths both sides; the judge reproduced that `--show-toplevel` is physical while a cwd may sit under a symlink (`/var` → `/private/var`). Two wiring tests pass (5/5), and two mutants are killed. **Expected eval impact: none on scores.** Evals and mission pi runs use `pi --mode json`, and pi 0.85.1 binds extensions there with a no-op UI context (`runner.js:88-92`), so the warning never reaches the model. The only eval-visible change is one extra `git rev-parse` subprocess when the model runs `git add`, `stash`, `checkout`, `restore` or `reset`. **Also needed:** `cmd/ailang/pi_assets/unowned-dirty.ts` is a `make pi-assets` copy (byte-identical at HEAD), and that path is outside fleet scope. **Options:** A, approve; the fleet lands the `.pi/extensions/**` diff, and the `pi_assets` sync goes to V1 or an attended session. B, approve and widen fleet scope to that one `pi_assets` file, so the fleet lands both. C, leave it unfixed (the warning shows only in interactive pi sessions). **Recommend A.**

**`stall:watchdog:slow-on-hung-tool` (stapledon, 10-07): ask 1 is a ghost of #1391. Should ask 2, a shorter no-progress threshold for pi controllers, still be built?** Measured at iteration 71 on `d45cf4e6b`; an independent sonnet judge reproduced every number (PASS-WITH-EDITS 78, edits applied). **Ask 1: yes, the cap reaches them.** #1391 (`7eaf9bece`, 2026-09-29 07:24Z) loads `tools/pi-extensions/controller-bash-cap.ts` with `-e` on the driver's one pi controller spawn (`mission-control.sh:2480`; the resume path reuses it, and the other pi calls are `--no-tools` probes). It clamps every pi bash call to 540 s (`MISSION_PI_BASH_CAP_S`), inside the 600-s window, and `test_driver_notify.sh:1003` pins the wiring. The stapledon 09-28 `find ~ -maxdepth 6` hang predates it. **Ask 2 is yours.** The sample count and 600-s budget are ruled by D-FLEET-4/-7 ("sample counts and the 600 s budget stay unchanged"). The 2400-s `STALL_GRACE` and `STALL_CHILD_AGE` are set past the skill's 30-min bounded-wait cap (`mission-control.sh:1117-1127`). A pi-only change would re-open both. **Data:** since #1391 the slot-verdict ledgers of all 7 missions hold 133 pi-controller slots. 30 got past fire-time capacity admission (18 of those then paused for capacity), and exactly one was KILLED: the ticket's own fleet 10-04 event (`KILLED_at=gate-5`, elapsed 5217 s). That was a model-side stall after a tool result, which no bash cap can bound. It came at gate 5, far past the 40-min grace, so a shorter grace would not have changed it. Fewer samples would have saved at most 240 s (3 samples) to 360 s (2 samples) of its 600-s window. 30 slots and 1 kill bound A's evidence; they do not prove A is unneeded. **A:** the fleet designs pi-only thresholds (a shorter grace, with `STALL_CHILD_AGE` to match, and/or fewer samples when `CONTROLLER_PROVIDER=pi`). **B (recommended):** waive ask 2 and resolve the ticket citing `7eaf9bece`. The cap removes the hang shape the ticket describes, the one post-cap kill would not have been shortened by a smaller grace, and a wrong kill costs a whole iteration. Default until answered: thresholds unchanged (the current state). Evidence: `fleet-mission-evidence/iteration71/`.

**`pi:openrouter:uncapped-max-tokens-402` (stapledon, 10-07): the output caps for three routed OpenRouter models live only in the rig's installed pi config. Who adds them to the repo, and should a 402 'can only afford' read as config?** Measured at iteration 72 on `490fb730b`; an independent sonnet judge verified every claim (PASS-WITH-EDITS 80). `tools/pi-extensions/models.mission.json` has no `openrouter` entry for `z-ai/glm-5.3`, `moonshotai/kimi-k3` or `minimax/minimax-m3`. The installed `~/.pi/agent/models.json` carries all three at `maxTokens` 32000 (attended 10-07 workaround). All three are still routed as role fallbacks (designer, planner, evaluator; `mission-control.sh:1391`, `:1503`, `:1634`); the OpenRouter GLM controller rung was retired 10-07. Root cause, found by the judge: `internal/executor/pi/config_preflight.go` checks the installed config only for models whose task carries registry settings, and these three have no registry rows, so nothing holds them. Both files are outside fleet scope, and reclassifying `^402:` (`RUNTIME_QUOTA_SIG`, `:1152`) is D-FLEET-11/13 policy. No `can only afford` line in any retained driver log (since 10-27; control fired). A fleet-side probe was considered and rejected: warn-only would duplicate the preflight, and skip/demote would change lane order. **Recommendation A**: the owner of `tools/pi-extensions/` and `internal/modelreg/models.yml` (V1/attended) adds registry rows with `max_output_tokens` and matching `models.mission.json` entries for the three models (32000 is the installed value; confirm the non-GLM two with `scripts/check_pi_wire_budget.sh`), so the drift test and the preflight hold them. Keep `^402:` as capacity: the oversized request is not formed while the cap is installed. Then the fleet resolves the ticket. **B**: also reclassify `can only afford` as config. Default until answered: the ticket stays open and nothing changes.
